title: Simple RAG: Answers from Documents
why: “How do I cancel a booking?”, “I'm allergic to nuts” — the answer isn't in the menu but in the restaurant's PDFs, and the model doesn't know it. Putting the whole document into the context is expensive, fine-tuning is expensive and has no sources. RAG is exactly for this kind of task: the chatbots of banks, clinics and public services, internal knowledge assistants — they all work this way. Today we build our first complete RAG: PDF → parts → search → an answer with a source.
outcomes: You'll explain RAG's two pipelines (ingestion and query) and why it beats the whole document in the context and fine-tuning
You'll extract text from a PDF page by page (PdfPig), cut it into parts with an overlap, and store the parts with vectors in a `DocumentChunk` table
You'll find the parts relevant to a question with a threshold and put them into the prompt as numbered sources
You'll plug RAG into lecture 7's chat: an answer with the source number, “I don't have information”, the original question in the history

review.q: Why don't we put the whole PDF into the context, and why don't we train the model (fine-tuning)?
review.a: The whole PDF — thousands of tokens on every question, slow, a large document doesn't fit, “lost in the middle” · fine-tuning — expensive, again on every change, it memorizes facts badly and can't name the source

review.q: What are RAG's two pipelines, and when does each one run?
review.a: ingestion — once, on upload: PDF → text → parts → vectors → database · query — on every question: vector → top 5 → prompt → an answer with a source

review.q: Why do we cut a document into parts, and what do we need the overlap for?
review.a: The vector of a whole document is the “average” of everything — blurry; a part = one idea, a precise vector and a cheap context · the overlap — the last sentence in the next part too, so an idea isn't cut at the boundary

review.q: Why do we need a threshold in RAG's search?
review.a: A search always finds something · without a threshold, for “a borscht recipe” the model would get 5 meaningless parts and might make something up · with a threshold — 0 parts and “I don't have information”

review.q: Why do we store the original question in the chat history and not the message with the sources (augmented)?
review.a: The sources are only for this request — others will be found next time · storing them in the history would inflate every message with 5 parts (the budget, lecture 7)

quiz.q: “How do I cancel a booking?” — why can't the model answer correctly without RAG?
options: Our restaurant's rules weren't in its training data — it either doesn't know or makes it up
quiz.explain: RAG gives the model a “book” at the exam.

quiz.q: Why isn't fine-tuning a good way for the restaurant's rules?
options: It's expensive and slow, again on every change, it memorizes facts badly and can't name the source
quiz.explain: Fine-tuning is more suitable for style and format than for facts.

quiz.q: Why do we use `ContentOrderTextExtractor` when extracting text with PdfPig?
options: A PDF stores letters with coordinates; it assembles them in reading order, while `page.Text` often glues words together
quiz.explain: On a scanned PDF both return nothing — OCR is needed.

quiz.q: We stored the whole 18-page document as one vector. What happens in the search?
options: It finds better — there's more text
The vector is the “average” of every topic — it's blurry and compares badly with a specific question; it also exceeds the limit
quiz.explain: That's why chunking — a part = one idea.

quiz.q: What is the overlap (the last sentence in the next part too) for?
options: So that an idea split between two parts isn't cut — both parts have a “bridge”
quiz.explain: The price — a little extra text in the database.

quiz.q: Why do we cut the text page by page?
options: So that every part has an exact page number — for citing the source
There are fewer parts this way
quiz.explain: The price — an idea split across pages stays in two parts.

quiz.q: Why do we give the sources numbers and the page `[1] (rules.pdf, p. 3)`?
options: The model writes the number in the answer — we know which file and page it is; the user checks, and we see which part was bad
quiz.explain: Citation — RAG's main advantage over fine-tuning.

quiz.q: Which message do we store in the chat history?
options: The augmented one — with the sources
The original question — the sources are only for this request and mustn't inflate the history
quiz.explain: On the next question other sources will be found.
